title: BETSE model: leak and Kir channels produce a hyperpolarized neural tube prepattern

fields.label: Label
fields.value: BETSE model: leak and Kir channels produce a hyperpolarized neural tube prepattern

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In a BETSE bioelectric model of the stage 15 Xenopus neurula, regional differences in K+ and Cl− leak permeability open Kir channels in the neural tube, producing a Vmem of about −50 mV there while the neural folds and ectoderm stay near −5 mV, matching observed embryonic Vmem patterns.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › Model of Vmem

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This results in open Kir channels in the hyperpolarized neural tube region leading to a Vmem pattern of approximately −50 mV in the neural tube region, while the lateral neural folds and ectoderm remain at ~−5 mV (Fig. 3a, e).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › Model of Vmem”. Scope: BETSE model of an anterior view of the stage 15 Xenopus neurula surface in 0.1× MMR

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-02: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.90

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a quantitative simulation result using public software and a detailed supplementary model specification. Regional voltages can be reproduced and compared directly with the article's empirical calibration measurements.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run the published BETSE neurula model with the stated regional leak permeabilities, Kir channels, ionic medium, and gap junctions, then extract Vmem by region. The claim is confirmed if the neural tube approaches -50 mV while folds and ectoderm remain near -5 mV and the pattern matches measured voltage maps.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Regional permeability assumptions are calibrated rather than independently derived.

Exact software-version differences may affect numerical details.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.98
data existence: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: BETSE and neurula geometries are public, and the paper tabulates starting concentrations and the leak-and-Kir mechanism, so the voltage pattern can be recomputed. The exact 2018 configuration is not a file in the repository, and the match to real embryos rests on the paper's images. The simulation half is therefore testable with reconstruction, short of a turnkey reproduction of the published run.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rebuild the stage-15 anterior neurula in BETSE with the published ion concentrations, regional potassium and chloride leak, and Kir conductance, and test whether neural-tube Vmem is near −50 mV while folds and ectoderm stay near −5 mV. Closing Kir, or equalizing the leaks, should remove that contrast if the stated mechanism is required.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The spatial leak map is described with a figure and supplement rather than a deposited configuration file.

Agreement with embryonic voltages uses the paper's own images, which are not an independent recording archive.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.84
data existence: 0.68
data adequacy: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.62
